title: Origin with soy de
explanation: Use soy de plus a country or city to say where you are from. Keep de in the pattern; it is part of the meaning.

title: Asking origin
explanation: Use ¿De dónde eres? to ask one person where they are from. De dónde asks for origin, not current residence.

title: Residence with vivo en
explanation: Use vivo en plus a place to say where you live. Use soy de for origin and vivo en for residence.

title: Asking residence
explanation: Use ¿Dónde vives? to ask where one person lives.

title: Languages with hablo
explanation: Use hablo plus a language to say what language you speak. Use hablas in the question to ask another person.

title: A little with un poco de
explanation: Use hablo un poco de plus a language for limited ability. Keep de before the language.

title: Question accents
explanation: In direct questions, qué and dónde are written with accents. Spanish direct questions also begin with ¿.

title: Short personal identity profile
explanation: A tiny profile can combine name, origin, residence and languages with short sentences.
examples: Me llamo Marta. Soy de Ucrania. Vivo en Kyiv. Hablo ucraniano y ruso.

title: Origin and residence are different
explanation: Soy de tells where someone is from. Vivo en tells where someone lives now. Do not swap the patterns when the prompt asks for one specific meaning.
